segments.text: You send a request, then the reply disappears. In this example, the service already committed the write. The caller sees a timeout, but can't see that hidden outcome.
segments.visual: Send request; commit effect; lose reply. Explicit evaluator-only label on effect.

segments.text: The same timeout could also mean nothing committed. Those two histories look identical to the caller. A missing or stale lookup doesn't necessarily resolve the uncertainty.
segments.visual: Split into zero-commit and one-commit histories with identical caller timeout.

segments.text: Now retry the same request ID. With no deduplication, this toy produces two effects. A retained, durable, payload-bound key prevents the duplicate here. If the key has expired, the duplicate can return.
segments.visual: Reveal no-dedup, retained durable payload-bound key, expired key rows sequentially. Animate effects per narration.

segments.text: This is an atomic, sequential toy with no late original request. Real recovery also depends on freshness, expiry, and in-flight work. When the evidence can't settle the outcome, preserve unknown.
segments.visual: Scope card: atomic / sequential / no late original, then preserve unknown.
